name: THE DISTRIBUTION WAREHOUSE
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 453, 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428 (roofs and cover); ask row 468's list, the sixth: 'A DISTRIBUTION WAREHOUSE (North Las Vegas' industrial parks): racks as walls, lanes, the loading docks, forklifts.'
facts: North Las Vegas' industrial parks are the valley's real warehouse land: fulfilment and distribution buildings of several hundred thousand square feet to over a million each, so a fight takes one corner of one floor: four lanes of racking and a stretch of the docks.
A house tile is about 18 m: one tile of lane here stands for the three or four real aisles that fit in it, the way one tile of the hall stands for a block of cots.
Selective pallet racking runs in long straight rows with cross-aisles; a cross-dock building has dock doors down both long walls and little racking between: the two layouts.
The map's own kind 'warehouse' (engine/bohemia_fight_kinds.js: the industry zone, a works building of two and three storeys) is where it is fought.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (warehouse_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The warehouse district is the valley's distribution land: half its fights that are not on the rail yard's own cells go inside one, by the cell's own dice; the plain industrial blocks one in five (most of those are works and yards). The rest are fought outside, on the zone's own board.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words).

wall.effect: The warehouse's outer wall: no way through.

rack.effect: Pallet racking, five levels up, loaded: no way through, no sight through. The lane beside it and the gaps at its ends are the ways.

floor.effect: A lane between the racks, or the dock's apron: open floor, nothing to hide behind, and a gun sees down the whole lane; on AUTO nobody stays on it.
floor.say: The lane: open floor, and a gun sees down it.

pallets.effect: Pallets pulled out into the lane, still wrapped: cover.

spill.effect: A bay of the rack come down into the lane: cover.

camp.effect: Somebody sleeps between the racks: bedding and what they took off the shelves. Low cover.

drums.effect: Drums and cones left where the shift stopped: low cover.

forklift.effect: A forklift, its battery long gone: nobody stands on its tile; cover for the tiles beside it.

trailer.effect: A trailer still backed to its dock: nobody stands on its tile; cover for the tiles beside it.

conveyor.effect: The conveyor line: you climb over it, slow going (3 AP a step), and it is low cover.
conveyor.say: The conveyor: slow going, low cover.

cage.effect: The lock-up cage for what was worth stealing, cut open: cover.

column.effect: A column: nobody stands on its tile.

fire.effect: A fire in a drum somebody keeps. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A drum fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

dock.effect: A dock door, rolled up: open floor, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
dock.say_lit: A dock door: open floor, and the day is on you.

high.effect: The pick mezzanine, half a storey up: high ground, and nobody's at the bell. A blow or a shot down from it lands easier, one up at it harder; a gun reaches a tile farther from it. Up the stairs it is a walk; over its rail from the floor it is a climb: no attack that turn, and a beast cannot.
high.say: The mezzanine: you hit down easier, and a gun reaches a tile more.

high_pallets.effect: Pallets on the mezzanine: cover, on high ground. The best ground in the warehouse.
high_pallets.say: Pallets on the mezzanine: cover, and high ground.

high_desk.effect: Drums on the mezzanine: low cover, on high ground.
high_desk.say: Drums on the mezzanine: low cover, and high ground.

ramp.effect: The stairs: the WALK up to the mezzanine. A step onto them from the floor costs one more; a man who walks up can still strike this turn.
ramp.say_before: The stairs: the walk up, and you can still strike.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK FIVE's own picture for it is in warehouse_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL, RAIL, HEIGHT); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile. A DRESS piece is drawn and never counted.

say.height: The mezzanine: you hit down easier, and a gun reaches a tile more.

start_why: NOBODY HOLDS THE MEZZANINE AT THE BELL: both lines start on the floor, in the lanes; the pick mezzanine is whoever takes the stairs first.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the warehouse's roof deck and its open-web joists over the board at this alpha (10%, never past the fight's own most). 'src' is the picture COOK FIVE makes (see garage.json's ceiling); 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in.
